claim: John Muir led the fight against the damming of the Hetch Hetchy Valley as a reservoir for the city of San Francisco.

evidence.quote: John Muir, the leading preservationist of his day and founder of the Sierra Club, led the fight against the damming of the Hetch Hetchy Valley as a reservoir for the city of San Francisco.
Yesterday, December 19, was the centennial of the Raker Act, the bill that allowed the building of a dam in the Hetch Hetchy Valley.
John Muir, who led the opposition, wrote beautifully about the valley, calling it “one of Nature's rarest and most precious mountain temples.”
In the end, the Raker Act became law on December 19, 1913 and San Francisco celebrated its new water security, a pristine watershed preserved in a national park.

evidence.quote: The Scottish-born naturalist, conservationist, and writer John Muir (1838-1914)
John Muir (1838 –1914) was a Scottish-born American naturalist, author, and early advocate of preservation of wilderness in the United States.
Born in Scotland, John Muir emigrated with his family in 1849, settling at Fountain Lake, near Portage, Wisconsin.
A Scottish-born journalist and naturalist, John Muir (1838-1914) studied botany and geology at the University of Wisconsin (1861-1863).
He was a Scottish-born American naturalist, author, and an advocate for the preservation of wilderness in the United States and the National Park Service.
